metaTitle: Vacuum, Floor Washer or Carpet Cleaner? 2026 Buying Guide
metaDescription: Dust, sticky spills or stains? Find the right machine in three questions: a vacuum, a hard-floor washer or a carpet cleaner, plus a robot height check.
h1: Vacuum, Floor Washer or Carpet Cleaner: Which Machine Do You Need?
intro: Most floor-care mistakes start with the wrong kind of machine, not the wrong model. Dust and crumbs call for a vacuum, sticky spills and winter salt residue on sealed floors call for a hard-floor washer, and stains in carpet or upholstery call for a carpet cleaner. Pick your path below, or answer three quick questions to get there. Each guide then compares a machine only with others that do the same job.

sections.h2: Dust, crumbs and hair: dry vacuuming
sections.linkLabel: Compare stick, upright and robot vacuums
sections.html:
Who it's for: every home, on every floor. Dry vacuuming is the everyday routine, and it's the safe choice on unsealed or water-sensitive wood. Some hardwood makers warn against wet mops on their floors.

Typical messes: dust, crumbs, pet hair, sand and grit tracked in at the front door, dust bunnies under the bed and the couch.

Machine types:

  • Cordless stick vacuums for quick daily pickups, stairs and the car; many convert to a handheld.
  • Corded upright vacuums for carpet-heavy homes, with no battery to run down.
  • Robot vacuums that run on a schedule; with a self-emptying dock, you empty the dust bin far less often. Measure the clearance under your furniture first (question 3 below).

sections.h2: Sticky spills and dried-on dirt: hard-floor washing
sections.html:
Who it's for: homes with sealed hard floors such as tile, vinyl and sealed hardwood, especially kitchens, front entrances and mudrooms, and homes with kids or pets. For laminate, check that its maker allows damp cleaning. Not for carpet, and not for unsealed or water-sensitive wood.

Typical messes: sticky juice and pop spills, dried-on food under the table, muddy paw prints, salt residue and slush tracked in from outside in winter, grime that a vacuum can't lift.

Machine types:

  • Wet dry vacuums (hard floor cleaners) that vacuum and wash in one pass, with a clean water tank and a separate dirty water tank.
  • Robot vacuum and mop combos that keep sealed floors fresh between deeper cleans.
  • Steam mops that clean sealed floors with steam from plain water. Check your flooring's care instructions before you use one on wood.

sections.h2: Stains, pets, carpet and upholstery: fabric cleaning
sections.html:
Who it's for: homes with wall-to-wall carpet, area rugs, carpeted stairs or a fabric couch, and anyone with pets or small kids. It's also the path for car seats and floor mats.

Typical messes: pet accidents (urine, vomit), spills that soaked into the fibres, lingering odours, dingy traffic lanes on carpet, salt stains on car floor mats.

Machine types:

  • Portable carpet and upholstery cleaners (spot cleaners) with a hose and a hand tool for the couch, stairs, rugs, pet beds and car interiors.
  • Upright carpet cleaners (full-size deep cleaners) for whole rooms and high-traffic areas.

Both spray water and formula into the fibres, then pull the dirty water back into a separate tank. Check the care instructions for your carpet or fabric first, and try a hidden spot before you clean the whole piece.

sections.h2: How to measure under your couch and bed
sections.html:
Slide a tape measure under the furniture and note the gap from the floor to the lowest point of the frame, in centimetres or inches. Measure in a few spots, since a centre rail or crossbar can sit lower than the front edge.

Then compare that gap with the robot's full height, laser turret included. On the Canadian manufacturer spec sheets we reviewed, robots with a laser turret on top stand 93.5 to 104 mm (about 3¾ to 4 in.) tall, and slim models with the laser built into the body 79.8 to 82 mm (about 3¼ in.). Basic robots without laser mapping can be slimmer still: one maker says its model passes under a gap of 73 mm (2.87 in.). Some models lower a retractable turret to slip under furniture.

In our robot guides, each height stays exactly as the manufacturer lists it, in millimetres, so every model is compared on the same figure. You can enter your clearance in centimetres or in inches: we convert it to millimetres before comparing.

sections.h2: Why we never compare carpet cleaners with hard-floor washers
sections.html:
They look alike, with two tanks, a brush and a trigger, but they do different jobs.

  • Different surfaces. A carpet cleaner is built for fibres: carpet, rugs and upholstery. A hard-floor washer is built for sealed surfaces; Tineco, for example, says its Floor One washers are for non-carpeted floors such as vinyl, tile and sealed wood, and answers “No” when asked whether they can clean carpet.
  • Different depth. A carpet cleaner pushes water and formula deep into the fibres and pulls it back out. A floor washer spreads a thin layer of water and solution with a spinning brush roll and picks the dirty water straight back up from the surface.
  • Different specs that matter. For a carpet cleaner: suction through the hose, the hand tools, tank size and how wet the fibres stay. For a floor washer: the brush roll, the self-cleaning cycle, edge cleaning, weight and battery runtime.
  • Little real overlap. Some floor washers can go over area rugs, but BISSELL's word for that is “refresh,” not deep clean.

So each machine is ranked only against its own kind, in its own guide. A single score across both would reward the wrong strengths.

chooser.question: What's on most of your floors?
chooser.helper: Not sure whether your wood floor is sealed? Check the flooring manufacturer's care instructions before you use any wet machine.

answers.label: Sealed hard floors: tile, vinyl, sealed hardwood
A mix of hard floors and rugs

chooser.question: Which mess bothers you most?
chooser.helper: Pick the mess you deal with every week, not the occasional disaster.

answers.label: Dust, crumbs, pet hair or tracked-in grit
Sticky spills, dried-on dirt or winter salt residue on hard floors
Stains, pet accidents or odours on carpet or upholstery

chooser.question: Robot vacuum: how much clearance is under your couch or bed?
chooser.helper: Measure from the floor to the lowest point of the frame, in centimetres (for example, 9 cm). Inches work too (for example, 3.5 in.): we convert your figure to millimetres and compare it with each robot's height as the manufacturer lists it, laser turret included.

answers.label: Under 8.4 cm (about 3¼ in.): only the slimmest robots fit, or plan on a cordless stick vacuum
8.4 to 10.7 cm (about 3¼ to 4¼ in.): slim robots first
Over 10.7 cm (about 4¼ in.): most robots fit, turret included

faq.q: Can a floor washer replace my vacuum?
faq.a: On sealed hard floors, partly: a wet dry vacuum picks up crumbs and spills as it washes. But it only works wet. Tineco says its Floor One can't be used without water for dry vacuuming, because that damages the brush roller. Carpet and unsealed wood still need a regular vacuum.

faq.q: Can I use a floor washer or steam mop on hardwood?
faq.a: Only if the floor is sealed and your flooring manufacturer allows it. Tineco lists sealed wood among the floors its Floor One washers can clean. Wood-floor makers can be stricter: Mirage, a Canadian hardwood manufacturer, tells owners not to use a wet mop, to wipe up spills right away and to sweep or vacuum regularly. Check your flooring's care instructions and warranty before you go wet.

faq.q: Can a portable carpet cleaner clean my couch?
faq.a: Yes, that's one of its main jobs. Portable models come with a hose and a hand tool for upholstery, stairs, pet beds and car interiors. Check the fabric's care label first and try a hidden spot. Finish with a few passes without spraying to pull out as much water as possible.

faq.q: Should I get a portable or an upright carpet cleaner?
faq.a: Go portable if your messes are spots: a pet accident, a spill on the stairs, the couch, salt stains on the car mats. Go upright if you want to clean whole rooms of wall-to-wall carpet or dingy traffic lanes. Corded models need a nearby outlet, so check the cord length against the room.

faq.q: Will a robot vacuum and mop handle sticky spills?
faq.a: It keeps sealed floors fresh between deeper cleans. Its onboard water tank is small, though. A big sticky spill is a job for a floor washer, which lifts the dirty water into a separate tank as it goes.

faq.q: Does a robot's height include the laser turret?
faq.a: Check that it does, and always compare your clearance with the full height. Models with a retractable turret list two heights, one with the turret raised and one with it lowered: on one Canadian spec sheet, 93.5 mm and 79.8 mm (3.68 in. and 3.14 in.). The lowered figure is the one that lets them slip under furniture.
